pr.title: Mint this repository's CI review tokens through the hosted service instead of a stored app key
pr.head: bbeee25e9bde410e36d95a12aee8f3e07fdb7b70

summary: Projector reviews this repository's pull requests in GitHub Actions. Each review posts as the Projector Review GitHub App, projector-review[bot], so the job needs a token for that app. Until now the workflow minted it from the app's private key, which was stored as the PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY repository secret.

This change has the job ask Projector's hosted service for the token instead. The job proves which repository and pull request it runs for with a GitHub OIDC token, a short-lived identity token GitHub Actions issues to a job that has the id-token: write permission. The service checks the installation's plan and returns a token scoped to the repository. No repository then holds a copy of the app's key.

Reviews still post as projector-review[bot], so review.reviewers and the projector/review status are unchanged. The action keeps its self-managed path, app-id with app-private-key, for repositories that register their own app.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The workflow edits match what project init --ci-review --ci-app projector generates for the hosted app.
  • The first review found that tests/test_ci.py still expected this workflow to pass the key secret. The second commit fixes the test.
  • The review of the second commit ran under the new workflow and posted as projector-review[bot], so the hosted token path works.
  • The third commit makes init unset review.ci_app_id when it switches to the hosted app, and drops the ID from this repository. An incremental review read that change, and the gate and the check job pass on this head.

groups.title: Request the review token from the hosted service
groups.kicker: The review workflow and the setting that records which app it posts as
intro: Both jobs in the review workflow, the one that reviews and the one that publishes the summary, call the repository's own actions/review action. Each now passes app: projector where it passed app-id and app-private-key. Each job also gains id-token: write, which lets the action's "Request the hosted service's token" step ask GitHub for the OIDC token.

.projector.toml records review.ci_app = "projector", the value project init reads to regenerate the workflow. This workflow runs the action from the checkout rather than from a release, so init treats it as edited by hand and leaves it alone. That is why the pull request edits it directly.

checks.text: Generated ci.body(..., "projector") and compared it with this workflow: the app input and id-token: write lines match in both jobs.

files.note: Both jobs pass app: projector in place of the app ID and key, and gain id-token: write.
Records ci_app = "projector", the hosted service's app, and drops ci_app_id, which the hosted app does not use.

checks.text: Settings are read from the default branch, so project config get review.ci_app keeps printing projector-review until this merges.

groups.title: Drop the old app ID when init switches to the hosted app
groups.kicker: What project init does with a self-managed app's ID once the hosted app replaces it
intro: A repository that posts reviews as an app it registered itself records two settings: review.ci_app, the app's slug, and review.ci_app_id, its numeric ID, which the workflow passes as app-id. The hosted service's app needs no ID, because the service mints the token. An ID left behind after a switch would read as the ID of the app reviews post as.

So when project init --ci-app projector records the hosted app and an ID is set, init now removes review.ci_app_id from the repository's .projector.toml and says so on standard error. Both CLI documents describe the step, and docs/review-in-ci.md adds that you can delete the PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY secret once the change merges.

files.note: init_ci_review unsets review.ci_app_id when it records the hosted app.

checks.text: ci_app returns ci.HOSTED_APP as both slug and app for the hosted service, so this branch never runs for a numeric ID. unset_value edits only the repository's .projector.toml, the file record_setting wrote the ID to.

files.note: Adds the removal of review.ci_app_id to what --ci-app projector does.
Says init removes the old ID, and that the key secret can be deleted after the merge.

groups.title: Test the workflow without a key and the dropped app ID
groups.kicker: The workflow key test, and a new test for switching to the hosted app
intro: test_the_app_key_reaches_only_the_step_that_mints_its_token guards against the app's private key leaking into a job's or a step's env, where every step of the composite action, install scripts included, could read it. It checks two workflows: one project init generates with an app ID, and this repository's own.

The test asserted that the only line naming PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY was the action's app-private-key input. This repository's workflow now names the secret nowhere, so the test asserts a subset instead: every such line must be that input, and a workflow with none passes.
A new test, test_switching_to_the_hosted_app_drops_the_old_apps_id, records a self-managed app, runs init --ci-app projector, and checks that ci_app_id is gone and that init reported unsetting it.

checks.text: Ran PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest tests.test_ci at this head: all 38 tests pass.

files.note: Changes the key check from equality to a subset, so a workflow that passes no key passes, and adds a test that switching to the hosted app drops the old ID.

checks.text: The subset check alone would also pass a generated workflow that dropped its key. The test just above it still asserts that a generated workflow with an app ID passes both app-id and app-private-key as inputs, so that case stays covered.
